parties.ourParty: The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company" — customer/licensee of HDI's site development and hosting services)

plans.note: No liability heading surfaced in the outline, but the operative body (sec-p0001) is only partially enumerated; scan the later articles (post-Section 5) for any cap, exclusion of consequential damages or disclaimer, and check whether any cap is one-way in HDI's favour. If nothing exists, treat as missing rather than deviation.

Hosting/development deals normally carry an IP-infringement indemnity from the developer (HDI). Search the unenumerated body for indemnity language, including any reciprocal indemnity that would push content/IP risk for the Deerskin Products onto us; verify direction before classifying.

Nothing in the visible outline restricts the Company's businesses or product sourcing. Confirm no covenant in the body restricting Deerskin from selling through other channels or sites before concluding absent; a presence rule with no clause is a non-issue for us.

Site development/hosting arrangements between affiliated parties often make HDI the sole host or sole channel for Deerskin Products. Check the Article 1 service-scope provisions (including sec-1.4 access terms) for any obligation that we host or sell exclusively through HDI; flag only if we are locked in without an exit.
No pricing or most-favoured-customer language visible. Direction rule: only flag if the body obliges the Company to extend HDI its best terms; an MFN running in our favour is left alone.

Not apparent in the outline; the nearest personnel provision is the project-manager appointment in sec-5.4, which is governance rather than a non-solicit. Confirm no employee non-solicit binding the Company elsewhere in the body.

The defined term "Termination Date" confirms termination machinery exists somewhere in the unenumerated body. Locate it and test whether the Company can exit on notice without penalty and whether HDI has a symmetrical or broader walk-away right mid-term.
Check the term provision associated with "Termination Date" for auto-renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any renewal repricing; a fixed term with no evergreen roll is compliant.

Boilerplate governing law/venue will sit in the miscellaneous articles at the end of the body, ahead of the signature block (sec-p0072). Confirm the chosen law is NY/DE/CA/England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration.

Look in the closing miscellaneous provisions for assignment/change-of-control language; given HDI and Deerskin are related entities, watch for a HDI termination right triggered by a change of control of the Company.

sec-1.4 (HDI providing the Company with access to systems/materials) is the most likely locus for ownership and data provisions; also scan the body for ownership of the developed site, customer lists and order data. Flag any assignment of Company content, Deerskin Products IP or customer data to HDI.

Any licence back to the Company for the developed site, software or hosted platform will sit with the access provisions in sec-1.4 or the development article; test scope (affiliates and contractors) and whether it is revocable at will.

No audit heading visible. If an audit/inspection right appears in the fees or records provisions, check notice, frequency, off-site preference and who bears cost; rights running in our favour are not flagged.
Direction rule: only relevant if the body imposes liquidated damages, penalties or shortfall fees on the Company. Service credits or performance remedies running to us need no comment.

Check the development/hosting service articles for any HDI performance warranty, service levels or uptime commitment and its duration and remedy; a bare disclaimer with no affirmative warranty is a deviation.
No insurance provision surfaced. HDI hosts our site and handles customer/order data, so the rule is engaged; if truly absent from the body, mark missing and note the standard coverages.
No fee schedule or volume commitment visible in the outline. Check the compensation provisions for minimum fees, guaranteed volumes of Deerskin Products or take-or-pay mechanics binding the Company.

Given the defined "Termination Date", check the termination article and the sec-1.4 access provisions for post-termination return of Company data, customer lists and site content plus migration assistance; if only access-during-term is addressed, the rule is missing.
